dedupe_keys.name: montpellier how coexisting short and long supply chains shape the resilience of a city s food supply

description: This case study proposes and tests a way to characterise a city's food supply system and analyse its resilience, applied to Montpellier in southern France, a signatory of the Milan Urban Food Policy Pact. The authors, from INRAE, CIRAD, Institut Agro Montpellier, the University of Montpellier and FR CIVAM Bretagne, drew on economic and network sociology, management science and geomatics to describe the supply system as a social and spatial network of operators moving different products, and collected primary data from a range of sellers and their suppliers. The article was published in 2020 and is free to read online on the publisher's site and in PubMed Central, with no licence stated. Coverage is one city and its supply basin. Caveats: the survey data are not published, and the analysis is a snapshot before the COVID-19 disruptions. The results confirm that short and long supply chains complement each other, and show more broadly that the combination of three spatial markets favours the resilience of the city's supply, although it is also a source of vulnerability. Simulation uses: a network structure of urban food supply chains for disruption and resilience models. Related records: the Baltimore food system resilience planning (case_study-baltimore-food-system-resilience-planning) and the FAO City Region Food Systems programme (case_study-fao-ruaf-city-region-food-systems-programme) address urban food supply resilience elsewhere.
